sentences.text: Roseburia intestinalis was proposed as a novel species for butyrate-producing, anaerobic, Gram-positive strains isolated from human faecal material, described as slightly curved rods motile by multiple subterminal flagella.
The description reports that the species shows net acetate utilization during growth on media containing carbohydrates and short-chain fatty acids.

A study reported that Roseburia intestinalis expresses two gene loci conferring metabolism of beta-mannans, plant cell wall polysaccharides commonly found in human diets, calling it a primary degrader of this fibre.
Another study reported that Roseburia intestinalis was significantly depleted in stools of 444 patients with colorectal cancer compared with 575 healthy controls.
